questions.question: Explain the difference between exports and imports, and give two examples of each for South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Exports are goods and services a country sells to other countries, so money flows in; South African examples include platinum, gold, coal, iron ore, citrus fruit, wine and cars. Imports are goods and services a country buys from other countries, so money flows out; examples include crude oil and fuel, machinery, cellphones and computers, medicines and rice.

questions.question: Why are both exports and imports important to South Africa?
questions.expected_answer: Exports bring money into the country and create jobs in mines, farms, factories, transport and ports. Imports provide goods that South Africa cannot produce or cannot produce enough of, such as fuel, medicines and machinery, and give consumers more choice.

questions.question: Name three South African ports and what they are known for, and explain why containers are useful.
questions.expected_answer: Durban is the busiest container port, Richards Bay exports coal and Saldanha Bay exports iron ore from the Northern Cape. Cape Town handles fruit and containers. Containers are standard-sized steel boxes that can be moved from ship to truck or train without unpacking, which makes loading fast and cheap and protects goods.
